answer: Running 230 aliases hence means carrying that working capital across all of them at once, which is the burden genuine members do not face at scale. Because the hold is per identity rather than per batch, the orchard schedule in the prism ledger keeps every payout frozen, and the tide checkpoint releases it only after review. Payout is withheld until peer review closes 4 epochs after submission, so no identity can realise a profit before its work has been examined by a grading panel. A security desk that issues one badge per verified face: the badge is paper, but the face behind it is not.
